title: litmus result record, format_version 1
description: The root RunResult.to_json() payload written to result.json in a run directory. The structural view of a run: the summary tree with a per-node link into the temporal view (timeline.jsonl). Framework-owned objects stay open so a consumer accepts fields added within version 1 by a later release; docs/inspector-json.md carries the policy.

format_version.description: Result-record schema version. A consumer reads this field first and refuses a version it was not written for.

state.description: The terminal state of the root node.

failure.description: JSON-safe framework failure recorded on the root node, including nested causes. Null on Pass.

timeout.description: Structured time-budget evidence when a deadline determined or contributed to the state.

test_case.description: Stable name of the root node.

ancestor_names.description: Root-to-this path, inclusive. The durable node identity; names may contain '/'.

bread_crumbs.description: Display path, exactly ancestor_names joined with '/'.

summary_tree.description: Recursive snapshot rooted at this node.

physical_location.description: PHYSICAL_LOCATION from the run environment, or 'unknown' when absent.

env.description: Environment snapshot taken at run start, filtered by the run's allow or deny list. No variable is guaranteed present.

measurements.description: Framework-owned slot reserved for the parametric-measurement protocol. Empty in version 1; no statistical semantics may be inferred from its presence.

run_data.description: Detached structured evidence snapshot. Suite-authored keys beyond the reserved slot are permitted.

state.description: The three terminal states. There is no fourth; a pending node is represented by null where nullability is allowed.

nodeType.description: Framework-owned node-shape discriminator; the composition vocabulary of build_suite.

name.description: The failure class name: TestFailure, ContractViolation, FrameworkContractViolation, MissingVerdict, ExternalIntegrationFailure, OperatorInterrupt, or a suite-defined TestFailure subclass.

state.description: The terminal state this failure produces on its node.

expected.description: JSON-safe rendering of the expected value, when the failure carried a comparison.

received.description: JSON-safe rendering of the received value, when the failure carried a comparison.

banner.description: Escalation banner on contract violations and missing verdicts.

node.description: Name of the node a contract violation or missing verdict happened in.

bug.description: Present and true when broken code, not hardware, produced the failure.

cause.description: JSON-safe rendering of the underlying exception, when there is one.

returned.description: JSON-safe rendering of the non-verdict a node returned.

operator.description: Present and true when the operator interrupted the run.

signal.description: Name of the POSIX signal that interrupted the run.

failure.description: A framework failure rendered through its to_json() method. Open: a TestFailure subclass may add fields, and a reader falls back on name, fail_message, and state.

budget_seconds.description: Positive finite duration declared on the winning clock.

elapsed_seconds.description: Active window time consumed when that clock fired.

clock.description: Root-to-declaring-node path of the winning clock.

timeout.description: Evidence emitted when a time-budget clock cut a subtree.

state.description: Terminal state, or null when the node was declared but never ran.

failure.description: JSON-safe failure for this exact node.

timeout.description: Structured time-budget evidence for this exact node.

log_path.description: POSIX path of this node's timeline.jsonl relative to the run directory. Null when the node never ran or its records rolled up into an ancestor; the root always carries one.

children.description: Ordered child nodes; groups retain declaration order after settlement.

summaryTreeNode.description: One node of the structural view.
